name: Stinson 108 Voyager
summary: Postwar four-seat, fabric-covered high-wing tourer with a six-cylinder Franklin engine; built by Stinson, then Piper, in numbers above 5,000.

wings: High wing braced by one strut per side
Partial leading-edge slots forward of the ailerons
engines: Fixed-pitch two-blade propeller in a rounded cowling
fuselage: Four-seat cabin with one large door each side and rear side windows
Fixed main gear with a tailwheel

tellTales: Four-seat fabric high-wing taildragger with a long, rounded cowl
Large, curved tail with a tall rudder
Single strut each side above a roomy cabin

confusedWith.howToTell: The Stinson 108 has a fabric fuselage and a curvier tail with a large rounded fin; the 170 is a metal fuselage with a straighter, upright fin and flat spring-steel legs.
The Stinson has an older rounded cowl for its Franklin flat-six and a curved tail; the Sedan has a squarer boxy cabin and all-metal wings.
The Stinson is a four-seater with a deeper cabin; the PA-12 is a three-seat Cub-style aircraft with a rounded Cub tail.
The Stinson has a fabric rounded fuselage and a curved fin; the 180 has an all-metal fuselage and a swept, angular fin.
